question:
A 30-year-old woman was found lying down and unresponsive by her parents 2 hours ago. She has no significant medical history. Two years ago, the woman discovered that her husband of 8 years was having an extramarital affair; this revelation subsequently resulted in a drawn-out divorce. After the separation, she moved back in with her parents, who note that she stays in her room, sleeps a lot, and rarely eats. A physical exam shows obtundation. Her temperature is 37.1ºC (98.7ºF), pulse is 110/min, respirations are 24/min, and blood pressure is 126/78 mm Hg. The patient’s admission labs are as follows:
TSH  3.2 µU/mL
Morning cortisol  8 µg/dL
Prolactin 15 ng/mL
FSH 7 mIU/mL
LH 6 mIU/mL
Glucose 22 mg/dL
C-peptide not detected
Beta-hydroxybutyrate  ≤ 2.7 mmol/L
Which of the following is most true of the cell type that is likely involved in the production of the molecule causing this patient’s symptoms?

options.opa: Contains M3 receptors that stimulate Gq in response to parasympathetic innervation
options.opb: Gram-negative enteric bacillus; catalase-positive, oxidase-negative, turns pink on MacConkey agar
options.opc: Located in the periphery of islets of Langerhans
options.opd: Located in zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex
options.ope: Gram-negative enteric bacillus; urease-positive, oxidase-positive, can be identified by silver stain

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Glucose 22 mg/dL -> Hypoglycemia -> Neuroglycopenic symptoms -> 95% CHAIN: Hypoglycemia -> Insulin deficiency -> Beta cells dysfunction -> 90% CHAIN: Beta cells dysfunction -> Decreased insulin secretion -> Reduced glucose uptake -> 85% CHAIN: Reduced glucose uptake -> Brain deprived of energy -> Obtundation -> 80% CHAIN: Obtundation -> Altered mental status -> Unresponsiveness -> 75% CHAIN: Unresponsiveness -> Lack of response to stimuli -> 70% CHAIN: Lack of response to stimuli -> Possible coma -> 60% CHAIN: Beta cells dysfunction -> Decreased C-peptide -> 80% CHAIN: Decreased C-peptide -> Reduced endogenous insulin production -> 75% CHAIN: Reduced endogenous insulin production -> Increased blood glucose -> 70% CHAIN: Increased blood glucose -> Glycosuria -> 95%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms of hypoglycemia, which is likely due to an insulin-secreting tumor called an insulinoma. Insulinomas are neuroendocrine tumors that arise from the beta cells of the pancreas, which are located in the periphery of the islets of Langerhans.
